Adjusted geometric validation of selected miQC classifications

Source: R/geometry_adjustments.R
geometry_adjustments.Rd

Performs a post hoc geometry-based plausibility check of a selected miQC classification. Cells may be reassigned when their current keep/discard status is inconsistent with the fitted model curves.

Usage

geometry_adjustments(
  df,
  model_type,
  rescue_quantile = 0.5,
  discard_quantile = 0.95,
  converge_quantile = 0.05,
  safe_keep_dist = 1.25,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

df

The data.frame object for flexmix_data.

model_type

Character Scalar describing the model type used in run_miQCadj(). Available options include "one_dimensional", "linear", "spline", "polynomial", or "polynomial_raw".

rescue_quantile

Numeric between 0 and 1. Lower threshold used for rescuing discarded cells. Will be ignored for one-dimensional model. Defaults to 0.5.

discard_quantile

Numeric between 0 and 1. Upper threshold used for reassigning implausible kept cells. Will be ignored for one-dimensional model. Defaults to 0.95.

converge_quantile

Numeric between 0 and 1. Lower quantile of curve gaps used to define convergence regions. Will be ignored for one-dimensional model. Defaults to 0.05.

safe_keep_dist

Non-negative Numeric Scalar. Distance ratio favoring keeping cells. Will be ignored for one-dimensional model. Defaults to 1.25).

verbose

Logical Scalar. Whether information regarding reassignments should be printed. Defaults to TRUE.

Value

Named list with slot information for:

df

Updated data.frame with geometry-adjusted miQC.keep_geom_adj classification column and geometry-related columns miQC.geom_adj, miQC.geom_region, miQC.dist_up, and miQC.dist_low.

geometry_check

Adjustment thresholds used for geometry checks, including the specified function arguments.

Details

The function adds adjusted classifications and diagnostic measures to the provided data.frame and records thresholds and the number of reassigned cells in geometry_check.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
df_list <- geometry_adjustments(df=flexmix_data, model_type = "linear")
} # }
